lawyer:
Rezia Sultana Begum, Advocate ------ For the Plaintiff. 
Akmal Hossain, Advocate ------ For the Defendant.
parties:
Dr Subir Khiyang Babu ------ Plaintiff
Vs
Stamina Haider ------ Defendant
full_judgment:
Upon a notice issued by this Court vide judgment and order dated 23-7-2014, by which a Decree Nisi for dissolution of the marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant was passed in view of the provisions under section 10 of the Divorce Act, 1869 ("the said Act"), this matter has been taken up for hearing and disposal to determine whether the said Decree Nisi can be made absolute in view of the provisions under section 16 of the said Act. 

 2. Short facts, relevant for the disposal of this matter, are that the plaintiff-husband, professing Christian religion, filed an application under section 10 of the said Act before this Court for dissolution of the marriage between him and Ms Stamina Haider (defendant) contending, inter nun, that the said marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant was solemnized on 28-3-2008 in the Community Center, Gazipur in accordance with the provisions of the Christian Marriage Act, 1872. That the said marriage was conducted by one Mr Bishop Joha Hira (Pastor), Government Christian Marriage Register, Calvary Apostolic Church, Bangladesh. After such marriage, though the parties lived their conjugal life for about one year, they did not have any kids. That, after such marriage, the plaintiff found that the defendant started to behave differently and she had started an illicit relationship with someone and, as such, continued to commit adultery. That though the plaintiff tried to bring her back to normal life, he failed. Thereafter, out of such dispute between the parties, they started living separately for about five years and then the plaintiff decided to dissolve the marriage in accordance with law and, accordingly; did so by swearing affidavit on 19-5-2013. Thereupon, the plaintiff filed the aforesaid application before this Court seeking Decree Nisi for dissolution of the said marriage. Upon such application, the defendant-wife entered appearance, but did not file any affidavit, statements, or counter-affidavit controverting the statements/allegations as contained in the said petition of the plaintiff. Thereafter, the plaintiff himself got examined himself as PW 1 by this Court and proved the concerned documents and, upon hearing the parties, this Court, vide judgment and order dated 27-3-2004, passed the Decree Nisi dissolving the said marriage and, theory, issued a show cause notice upon the defendant (allowing 6 (six) months time in view of the provisions of section 10 read with section 16) asking her to show cause as to why the said Decree Nisi should not be made absolute. Upon such notice, the defendant-wife has filed a reply and controverted the allegations made by the plaintiff in the original petition and further prayed for judicial separation instead of the dissolution of their marriage. 

 3. It has to be borne in mind that this Court is not disposing of any application under section 10 of the said Act, rather it is disposing of the application filed by the plaintiff under section 16 as well as the reply given by the defendant in order to determine whether the said Decree Nisi dated 23-7-2014 dissolving the marriage between the parties can be made absolute. Thus, at this stage, in view of the specific provisions of section 16 of the said Act, this Court is not allowed to reopen the dispute between the parties by entertaining the counter-affidavits or reply controverting the allegations in the original petition. The only scope open to the defendant at this stage is to draw the attention of this Court as regards any collusion by the parties or any material facts which were not brought before this Court while this Court was disposing of the application of the plaintiff under section 10. Therefore, at this stage, the statements in the defendant's reply controverting the allegations in the original petition of the plaintiff and making counter allegations against the plaintiff cannot be entertained. 

 4. Besides, it appears from record and the said Decree Nisi dated 23-7-2014 that the defendant had the ample opportunity before this Court to controvert those allegations or to make counter allegations before the Decree Nisi was passed. However, she opted not to do so and even refused to cross-examine the PW 1 while he was examined before this Court as a witness. Accordingly, this Court, in disposing of a petition under section 10 of the said Act, did not have any option but to hold that the statements made by the plaintiff and the documents submitted by the plaintiff were proved and, accordingly, this Court also did not have any option but to pass a Decree Nisi in view of the provisions under section 10 of the said Act. 

 5. Now, since no allegation of collusion between the parties has been made by the defendant in her reply and by way of such reply the defendant having not brought to the notice of this Court any material facts which were not before this Curt at the time of disposing of the petition under section 10, I am of the view that this Court, at this stage, cannot take into consideration those counter allegations or allegations of the defendant. Accordingly, this Court does not find any reason for reversing the said Decree Nisi dated 23-7-2014 passed by this Court. 

 6. In view of above, since legal requirements have been fulfilled and more than 6(six) months time has elapsed in the meantime after passing of the said Decree Nisi, this Court finds no reason as to why the said Decree Nisi should not be made absolute in view of the provisions under section 16 of the said Act. 

 Accordingly, the Decree Nisi dated 23-7-2014 passed by this Court under section 10 of the said Act is made absolute in view of the provisions under section 16 of the Divorce Act, 1869.
